correctness.rationale: Normalized monomial projection gives the +2 shift A_n=√[(n+1)/(n+3)] and the −1 shift B_n=√[n(n+1)]/(n+2), with absent entries zero. Commuting gives diagonal A_n²−A_(n−2)²+t²(B_n²−B_(n+1)²) and third off-diagonal t[A_n B_(n+3)−A_(n+1)B_(n+1)], where t=|b/a|. Rotation removes the relative phase. These agree with D_n,E_n,O_n. At t=2/3 the first three row lower margins are 59/405, 61/162 and 191/1050; for n≥3 the all-index rational lower margin is positive by shifting the numerator polynomial by n−3. The quadratic form is nonnegative on finite vectors by the row bound, and then by boundedness and density; decreasing t improves the same bound. For t>2/3, first choose a finite alternating chain length L so 4−3t²−4t(1−1/L)<0, then translate the chain to sufficiently high indices to produce a negative form. If a=0 and b≠0 the backward-shift diagonal is negative; the zero operator is normal. Boundary differentiation gives minimum Jacobian 4|a|²−4|a||b|−3|b|², and summability on the three bands proves trace class. The diagonal sums telescope to 2 and −1 for the two individual shifts, so the trace is 2|a|²−|b|². Replay: frozen RESULT.md proof §§1–4. The finite checker was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Fleeman–Liaw treat the opposite-angular monomials (m,n,i,j)=(2,0,2,1) in their general sufficient test. The endpoint check is a single rational polynomial sign after substitution; see direct implication below.

Revilla–Simanek §2 give the exact quadratic form for a radial-power symbol and §2.2 use blocks of ones at high monomial index to disprove positivity. The exact coefficients specialize to s=0 (the projection formula and its denominators are valid there; the paper itself uses exponent zero in §3).
Kim–Lee Theorem 2.9 covers these indices only with a weaker necessary inequality, |a|²≥(3/4)|b|².
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier sufficient theorem and the earlier necessary-test method with the published exact coefficients cover the claimed window together. The asymptotic-in-radial-power wording of Revilla–Simanek Theorem 1.4 does not by itself establish a cutoff at radial power T=1; it is the exact form (3) and its published block test that directly do so.

evidence: In Fleeman–Liaw Remark 3 put (m,n,i,j)=(2,0,2,1) and x=|a/b|=3/2. The first three comparison margins are 43/135, 83/270 and 211/2100; the rest have numerator 2(2k+5)(11k⁴+74k³+121k²−86k−216) over 3k(k+1)²(k+2)²(k+3)²(k+4)(k+5). The quartic has coefficients (11,206,1381,3826,3504) in descending powers of k−3 and is positive. The criterion stays satisfied for larger x, establishing prior sufficiency including equality.

For necessity set r=|b/a| and take n=2,m=1,s=0,T=1 in the Revilla–Simanek coefficients. Their monomial form has k³σ_k→4, k³ω_k→−3, and δ_k=2/[(k+3)(k+4)(k+5)]. On their block of L≥4 consecutive ones starting at N, the cross term in (3) has L−3 pairs (choose the phases on each chain to realize the negative sign). The N³/L-scaled limit is 4−3r²−4r(1−3/L). If the form is nonnegative for every block, then taking N large with L fixed and then L→∞ gives (2−3r)(2+r)≥0, hence r≤2/3.
The two coefficient-zero cases are elementary analytic and backward shift cases; the trace follows by ordinary telescoping of the same two shift diagonals.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: These are direct substitutions, polynomial arithmetic and the prior block test applied without discarding its diagonal term. Together they already furnish the submitted classification and, by factorization, the boundary-Jacobian equivalence. A different normalization of the endpoint row certificate does not supply a new classified range.

value.rationale: The concrete example is natural and can illustrate why checking only diagonal moments misses positivity. As an independent exact finding, however, its coefficient boundary is a routine specialization of a published sufficient comparison and a published high-index test in the same symbol family. Neither its algebraic boundary-Jacobian reformulation nor the telescoping trace yields an independently valuable new remainder.
